verdict.rationale: Linear's Loops let teams describe a job in plain language and run it on a schedule or in response to workspace events, such as changes to initiatives, projects and cycles. Documented actions include updating documents and posting Slack messages, so this is a first-party event-triggered automation capability. It is agent-driven rather than a deterministic rule builder, and the catalog of triggers and actions is only lightly documented. Webhooks and the API are developer building blocks and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: an explicit configurable trigger/condition/action rule builder, a documented full catalog of triggers and actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration that Loops reliably eliminate manual steps.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can build trigger-and-action automation rules to eliminate repetitive manual steps

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
When a project's target date changes, a loop can automatically update the launch plan and post a Slack message explaining what changed, why, and who needs to act.
